dedupe_keys.name: bacs statistics voluntary and mandatory cyber incident reports and reported vulnerabilities switzerland

description: The Swiss Federal Office for Cyber Security (Bundesamt für Cybersicherheit, BACS), which grew out of the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), publishes three sets of current statistics. The first counts cyber incidents reported voluntarily by the public and companies, including incidents spotted early that caused no damage, shown as linked interactive charts: weekly reports over the last twelve months, the most frequent incident types by main category and subcategory per week, and the yearly course of a chosen category. Weeks run Monday to Sunday and figures are updated on Tuesday mornings; from April 2026 phishing is broken down further, including voice phishing, phishing after classified adverts and callback scams. The second covers the incidents that operators of critical infrastructure must report to BACS, published for 2025 and 2026; the third covers vulnerabilities reported to BACS as the Swiss CVE numbering authority and the federal bug bounty programme run with Bug Bounty Switzerland. Coverage: Switzerland. Format and access: interactive web charts in German, French, Italian and English, free; no bulk download was found. Caveats: voluntary reports reflect reporting behaviour; mandatory reporting started in 2025, so series are short. Simulation uses: rates and types of cyber incidents against Swiss critical infrastructure for scenario design and threat exposure. Related records: CERT.br statistics are a comparable national series, and the BAKOM data describe Swiss networks.
